utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters, the registry staff, the counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for the Defence. We will resume our work, but before bringing in the witness, we have a decision to communicate to the parties, and particularly to the Defence of Mr. Zigic. And I apologise for the delay, but the Chamber had other obligations to deal with. The question that we wish to decide upon is the question of the expert witness, Dr. Barudzija. During a previous meeting, Mr. Stojanovic raised the question of his expert witness proposed, Barudzija. The Chamber heard the parties on the issue on the 19th of February, 2001. The testimony of Dr. Barudzija can be divided into two parts: In the first he would testify as a fact witness, and in the second he would provide his opinion in the capacity of an expert witness. The Prosecutor objected to the testimony of the doctor as an expert because he wouldn't be neutral. However, the Prosecutor does accept that he gives opinions if those do not exceed his expertise. The Chamber notes, in the first place, that there is nothing in the Rules preventing an expert witness from testifying also on certain facts which are a part of his personal knowledge. It finds that the Defence has the right to choose its expert witnesses and that this testimony will be admitted by the Chamber, evaluating its relevance and its probative value in accordance with the provisions of Rule 89(C) of the Rules. However, all statements by the expert witness must conform to the provisions of Article 94 bis of the Rules. The Chamber therefore rules that the Defence of the accused Mr. Zigic can call Dr. Barudzija both as a fact witness and as an expert witness, on condition that, as far as his expert testimony is concerned, the provisions of Rule 94 bis should be observed. That is the ruling of the Chamber. So I think now -- yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for the floor. I just want to inform the Chamber that we have not to date been served with any 94 bis statement by expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's a statement. But Mr. Stojanovic is aware of the time limits of Rule 94. There's no need to discuss that matter now. I want to make sure -- can I have the witness brought in now? Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Can we call the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you for your ruling. We will keep in mind the 21 days required. It's just a question of translation. We already have the finding, the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we can call the next witness. Mr. Usher, please have the witness brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DD/1. Can you hear me? I wish to remind you that you are continuing to testify under oath. You may be seated. Make yourself as comfortable as possible. Mr. Waidyaratne, your witness for the continuation of the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, I was asking questions from you about your detention yesterday in regard to your detention in the Keraterm camp. When you saw Mr. Zoran Zigic in the camp, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You had not seen him carrying any weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see or hear Mr. Zoran Zigic ordering any of the detainees to sing Serbian songs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't Zoran Zigic who ordered anyone to sing songs. I sang them myself of my own accord. I didn't sing Serb songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please, my question was, did any -- did you hear Mr. Zoran Zigic or see Mr. Zoran Zigic ordering any other detainees to sing Serbian songs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During your detention in Keraterm, did you see a person by the name of Ramadanovic -- sorry, Jasmin Ramadanovic detained in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: To make it much clear, you don't know him, you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Another matter concerning the Room 3 incident in Keraterm, you said that the people who were detained in Room 3 were from the Brdo area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you know the ethnicity of these people who were detained in Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Witness, after you left the camp you said that you went to Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In the year 1992, the latter part of 1992 and in 1993, did you see or meet Mr. Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In 1994 did you meet him or see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, as I said before. I saw him in mid-June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were detained in the Trnopolje camp; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifteen days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you describe as to what you saw in -- the people who were detained or kept in the Trnopolje camp, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. All the people who were there were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Approximately could you assess as to how many people were detained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really, I don't know. I know that there were a lot of us, but I can't tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me for a moment, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in Trnopolje camp, the time that you spent in Trnopolje camp, is it your position that you didn't see Mr. Zoran Zigic, or that you didn't know whether he came or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That concludes the cross-examination, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Deretic, any re-examination? You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, after a question from my learned friend from the

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: answer was, and I quote --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Wald draws my attention to something that you said, the name that you mentioned that you shouldn't have mentioned, so please take care.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It is a big mistake on my part. I do apologise to both the witness, the Chamber, and all those present. In any case, Mr. President, may I request that we go into private session for a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. Maybe it's preferable. [Interpretation] Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may continue, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that it was your duty in Keraterm to distribute food and water.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: On those occasions, were you ever led to hit any one of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hit them, but I was in charge of the food. I distributed the food. Some people would get it five or six times and some of them not once. And I would say to them, the Muslims, as I am a Muslim too, "It's better that I hit you lightly than they. If they beat you, they'll kill you. I'm telling you nicely. Move away. You've got your food. You can't come back to get it five times." I didn't really beat anyone, but that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: But were you in a position to be able to push someone away or to slap someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could push someone, but not hit anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was [redacted] with you every day when you were distributing food and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he work in shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: So would it happen sometimes that he wouldn't be there during the day because it wasn't his shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would be there when his shift was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who would assist you when he was not on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other soldiers. There were other soldiers who assisted us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In answer to a question from my learned friend opposite that on one occasion you went with Zigic near the new post office, as you said, in Prijedor, to fetch water, you mentioned the name Faruk.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you go to get water from that man's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said you don't know his surname.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said I don't know his surname, but I do know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what that man did in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you get some cigarettes from Zoran Zigic free to have a smoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran give cigarettes to other people to smoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He gave some to my brother, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What I meant was without them having to pay for it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were these soldiers and policemen, or were they detainees? Did he give them to detainees as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. He gave them to policemen, to soldiers, and to the detainees as well. He gave cigarettes around to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever happen to see Zoran Zigic give food to anyone in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I know that he would take it from the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who did he give the food to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were they soldiers and policemen or detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he make them pay for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you sold the cigarettes, did you sell the cigarettes just to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sold them to the police and to the soldiers as well as to the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you had occasion to see a diagram in front of you. You were shown a diagram, and you noted down the positions of the premises there. You then on that occasion, you indicated where two machine-guns were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask, Mr. President, that the usher place the same diagram on the ELMO because I have another question concerning that diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: About the machine-guns, can you take a look at this photograph once again and tell us whether you have correctly indicated the positions where those machine-guns were set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Deretic, you can't see the weighing-in device. I can't see it here, but I know that one of them was facing the Banja Luka-Prijedor road, and the other one was at the corner by the weighing-in machine. I can't see that weighing-in machine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may, I should like to present the witness with a coloured photograph, and as this is a photocopy which is on the ELMO, the witness might find it easier to get his bearings here because it's a better photograph and shows more contrast.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate on this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I apologise for interrupting, but I can see that this photograph has been assigned a number, D8/4, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wrote that in, Mr. President, yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but if the witness is going to mark this photograph, we might have to assign it another number. So Madam Registrar, could you give us a number for this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. It will be D8/4A.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you now locate the positions of those machine-guns in more -- more correctly? You have your pointer, so could you do that now, please. Could you indicate Room 3 first, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you show us where one of the machine-guns was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was in front of number 3, in front of number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was it closer to the room, Room 3, or closer to the fence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to the doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: But show us where the fence is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the fence round here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: So you could look at the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was near.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You mean near the fence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was opposite, number 3 opposite. The machine-gun was facing directly towards them, towards number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the weighing-in device on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance itself to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you show us the entrance, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Now, where is the weighing device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weighing device is here, located here on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I apologise for interrupting you once again, but when the witness says "here" and "there" and uses similar terms, for the record, we do not know what he means, so either the witness will have to specify and make a mark of some kind or use letters, or you yourself will have to describe the exact locality with respect to a point we know; otherwise, in the LiveNote we won't be able to ascertain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Looking at the rooms from the entrance, can you see anything? Show us the entrance, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side is there something located there, an object?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's the weighing-in machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was there a house or a hut next to that weighing-in machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In relation to Room 3, can you say where the machine-gun was located? Now you have indicated the weighing machine to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here, right at the corner, because the machine-gun went directly -- was directly facing towards Room 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: If you have a pen, could you indicate that spot for us, please. And would you place a "V" for vaga, or weighing-in device. Could you place a "V" for vaga, meaning weighing-in machine. Please take a look at the photograph and not the screen. Can you now locate the machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: So we're referring to the machine-gun that was pointed at Room 3. Please look at the photograph and indicate where it was. Put "M1," machine-gun one, "M1" for where it was. And can you tell us where the other machine-gun was? Or let me help you. Where was Room 1 and 2? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: So where was the other machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was faced towards number 3, and the other was pointing towards the Banja Luka-Prijedor road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But can you see the Banja Luka-Prijedor road on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Then can you locate the second machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was here by the fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember to the left of the entrance in Keraterm --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: -- was there a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I understand that my friend is trying his best to -- but he is now trying to point out the places. I would expect the witness to mark the place, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Deretic, we already have an M1. Now you want to locate the M2, so please ask the witness where M2 was. It was a machine-gun. Also, we need to indicate the entrance to the camp, so on the bottom half of the photograph or the left-hand side by indicating an arrow, perhaps we could -- and also we might indicate the Banja Luka-Prijedor road with "PB" and an arrow; otherwise, when reading the LiveNote, the transcript, we won't be able to have anything on record. So we need that kind of information on paper, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you once again show us the Prijedor-Banja Luka main road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And can you place the letter "B" for Banja Luka, or "BL," where that road is, on the road, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now show us where the entrance to Keraterm was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you please place a "U" for the entrance, "U," the letter "U," meaning Ulaz entrance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you now indicate the position of the second machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was here in front of number 3. You have already shown that. What do you want me to write here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Please write "M-2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I think that with the cross-examination by Mr. Waidyaratne there was some new information with respect to the numbering of the exhibits, so perhaps we could -- that is to say, the room, the rooms in the compound. So perhaps we could ask the witness to indicate where Rooms 1, 2, and 3 were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, would you mark Room 1 and the other rooms too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: As already -- I do not know as to how the witness is going to mark those rooms again, because already we have the number 1, 2, and 3. So he may have a different shade, that if it's going to be different from what he has already done. Thank you, Your Honour. That was to assist Your Honour's Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne, but I don't think there's any problem, actually, because he was marking this on a different exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark in where the WC was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: I see you've got "V." Could you add a "C" to the "WC."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think we need the photograph any more, but we should like to ask, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Deretic, but I would like to ask the witness something. Witness, you wrote in "1," "2," "3," and "4." What does that mean, "1," "2," "3," and "4"? What do those numbers denote?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the rooms, the second dormitory, the third and fourth dormitory, because there were four rooms where we slept in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also wrote in the letters "VC". What do the letters "VC" stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where we went to the toilet. It was the WC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Could you now indicate to us where the pallets were? You mentioned some pallets in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I show you with my hand, by pointing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were here. Do you want me to write down anything?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Write down a "P." The letter "P" that you have written in on the right-hand side of the photograph indicates the site of the pallets, is that right, where the pallets were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Deretic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence of Mr. Zigic will subsequently be tendering this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, you said at one point during your testimony yesterday that the people from Room 3 had gone mad. Can you explain what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was very hot, it was very warm weather, but they weren't allowed to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that that evening, that is to say, before the shooting started, you were having stomach problems and that you went to bed earlier than usual.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When was your room locked up that night? When did they lock you up that night? What time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 7.30 -- between 7.30 and 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who locked you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After the shooting started, were you asleep then? Were you still sleeping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: But did the shooting wake you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you see that at the door to Room 3 the tin or metal had been taken off, and when did you see the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 6.00 in the morning, when [redacted]came to fetch me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When the shooting woke you up, did you look through the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: At one point when you were collecting up the dead individuals, the Prosecutor mentioned a name and a surname. He said "Sead Jakupovic."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said that he could not collect up the dead bodies, and afterwards the Prosecutor asked you another question. You did not say why he couldn't collect up those dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't because he felt sick. He started to vomit and he started losing consciousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was he there while you were going about that job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went off to the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: While there was shooting in the Keraterm compound, were you awake the whole time, or when did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I woke up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see anything then, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object. My learned friend has already asked that question, and the witness had said, "I woke up, but I didn't look through the door." If he's trying to get the answer again, I object to that, Your Honour. If it's in the morning, it's different, but if it's during the night, the time -- the shooting, I object to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness said that when he woke up, he didn't look, but my question now is, as the witness said previously that the shooting lasted for several hours, in fact, two to three hours, I am just asking him now whether during the shooting, later on, he saw what was happening in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In the morning when I woke up, I saw people starting to flee from Room 3. And in front of number 2 you could see bodies, dead bodies, that morning when [redacted]came to fetch me down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see people running past your room while the shooting was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: While your brother was washing the truck, the truck that had returned after taking away the dead bodies, did he have any problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you explain to us what were those problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother was washing the truck, and a policeman came and took hold of my brother and began beating him up behind the truck. I turned up at that point and called the policeman, Cicic. I said, "Cicic, this one Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 wants to kill my brother." And Cicic made the other policeman go away from the compound and asked him who let him in, in the first place. And the policeman left, went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: My last question, yesterday you said that after four or five days after your arrival in Keraterm that you were interrogated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know that some people after these interrogation sessions, that is to say, those who were detained, had been sent home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what happened to start off with. Once they had questioned you up there, they would send you home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: So who were these people who were sent home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that my brother was supposed to have -- to go home, too. He was questioned on that day, and he was supposed to go home, but he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Deretic. Judge Fouad Riad has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning Witness, Witness DD/1. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'd like to have some more information from you if you are in a position to tell me about it. You just mentioned that you were distributing food to the detainees, among other things, and you told them, "It's better that I hit you lightly than they." Why did you have to hit them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't actually hit them. I just pushed them aside, because I knew that if I did not do that, they would beat me. So I didn't hit them actually, I just got hold of them and pushed them aside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They would beat you, the detainees would beat you when you bring them food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the detainees did beat me, as well. We struggled, we struggled. We fought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was there a kind of animosity between you and the Muslim detainees? You were a detainee yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So why would they beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because. Because they singled me out, and they would say, "That's him." Because otherwise, the Muslims would threaten me, and I didn't actually know why because I helped them in Keraterm. I helped them most while they were in Keraterm, because those same people who were in Prijedor, I saved them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you don't know the reason for this hostility. Was it perhaps because of the accusation of your brother having killed a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems that that would be so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What was this Muslim which he was accused of killing? Was he a patriot? Was he one of the fighters? What was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: He was a detainee, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And what was the accusation, if -- although it was wrong, but what was it that -- was it a personal fight, or was it something political?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political, because that, that Muslim is alive and his father is in Kozarac, in Prijedor. And his father visited us at home and asked my mother --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I understood that, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I understood that. But the accusation itself was that he killed another detainee. Was this detainee an important political person for the Muslims, to arouse their hostility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You don't know. But the fact is that there was some kind of hostility against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was the people running the camp who asked you to distribute food, or it was out of your -- the kindness of your heart?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, that's when the food began. Then they asked me to distribute the food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They chose you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was right by the door. I slept right by the door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, there was also perhaps there the incident of kicking Car, of Mr. Zigic kicking Car. Did the -- was there any follow-up of this kicking? I mean, he just kicked him and left him or kicked him and continued acting in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Zoran Zigic just hit him once. He kicked him in the backside and left, went outside the gate. I don't know where he went; I just saw him leave the Keraterm compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So what followed, the running around with the heavy machine and so on, Mr. Zigic had nothing to do with it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was the other one, I think, Duca - Duca or Duca - who did that, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether it was Duca, I just know it was a group of soldiers. And after Zoran --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you don't know who did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. All I know is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You were present, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic only kicked Car, as you said, in the bottom, or did he kick other people, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was Zoran in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just once, when Car had been brought with the 53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And in general, your observation, what was the importance of Mr. Zigic in the camp? Was he obeyed? Was he running the camp or just moving around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, he wasn't commanding the camp, running the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, he was not. But what was his role exactly? Could he help people? Could he punish them? Could he kick them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could help, and he did help us a lot, us Muslims. He helped all my brothers. He helped me especially, too. I could have been 10 feet under ground by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But apart from you and your brothers, what was his position towards the -- because apparently you were apart from the others. What was your position with the other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good. I just saw Zigic once, and I know I could move around Keraterm. And I would say if I had seen him, but I didn't see him, so I can't say I did if I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You gave two different descriptions of the revolt of people in Room 3. The first one, "I thought that they were trying to run away and they were shot"; but now you mentioned answering the Defence counsel that they were so hot that they wanted to go out of the room. So what was exactly the case of this? Were they trying to run away from the camp, or were they bursting out because of the heat and then shot out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were inside. They were inside and they started fighting, having a fight, struggling with each other. And I know when that number 3 was opened, I know that a Muslim, a young man, also a Muslim, poked him with a large pole. That was in number 3, and that was a Muslim doing it to a Muslim in one of those dormitories, in that dormitory when they started breaking down the lower panel to the door, and that's when they began to run away, run out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said it was unbearably hot, and they ran out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So and they just ran out. So was it meant to escape from the prison and that's why they were shot out, or just run out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they started to escape towards number 2 and number 1 dormitories. I saw that. I saw the bodies, and I saw them trying to escape. Towards number 4 by the palace, that's the direction they were trying to escape. I know when I collected up their dead bodies. I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Escape out of the prison, out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Escaping from Room 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in number 1 I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And did you see Mr. Zigic around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You didn't. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, at the end, at the end, Mr. Stojanovic. Thank you, Judge Riad. Madam Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness DD/1, I've got several questions to try and understand your testimony because it seemed that at one point you might be saying one thing and at another point another, and I want to make sure that I know which one you really are saying. Now, to begin with, on the cigarette business, when you were selling cigarettes for Mr. Zigic, did he tell you what price to sell them for, or did you just sell them for anything anybody might have? Who decided how much you sold the cigarettes for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what the price was that Zoran Zigic told me to sell them at. I know I sold them to soldiers, the reserve police, and the detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand. You answered my question: You said that Mr. Zigic told you what price to ask for the cigarettes. Okay. Now, when you were selling food for some of the guards, did you get anything in return for that? Now, Mr. Zigic gave you some cigarettes of your own in response for your selling the cigarettes, but you also told us you sold food for some of the guards. Did you get any money or any food for yourself or any kinds of privileges in return for selling the food for the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You just -- why did you do it? Because they told you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the day you said -- or I have in my notes that you said two different things. Tell me which you believe is the correct one. At one time you said that the day before the shooting they set up the two machine-guns that day, and another time you said in answer to one of the questions no special machine-guns were set up that day. Could you tell us now which of those two statements is the correct one? The machine-guns in front of room -- or that were in the direction on the sketch of Room 1 and Room 3, were they set up that day? Were they always there? It seemed as though you gave different answers at two different times.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They weren't set up immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So when you said, and I have it in my notes, that that day they set up two machine-guns, you were wrong and you take that back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the machine-guns were there before we arrived in Keraterm. Maybe you didn't understand what I said. Before we got to Keraterm, the machine-guns had already been in position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: We will check the transcript of that, but I have in my notes that you said something quite different. We will check the transcript and see what exactly you did say as to that. During the afternoon before the shooting, I want to make sure I have this correct, you didn't see Mr. Zigic anywhere around the camp. I believe that's what you said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when -- again, I had difficulty in understanding precisely what you were saying about what you saw the night and the next morning of the shooting. You said, I believe, that you went in to bed in Room 1, and you were awakened by the shooting. Now, you talked about seeing people fleeing. Are you -- did you see people flee that night? Did you see people flee the next morning? Did you only see the bodies in positions from which you inferred that they were fleeing? I didn't understand your answer as to what exactly you saw and when you saw it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the bodies as the men started to flee towards dormitory 2 and dormitory 1 because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. Let me just stop you there so that again I understand. It may be the difference in our languages and the translation that makes it difficult. Do I understand you now to say you never saw people actually fleeing. You saw bodies in positions from which you inferred that they must have been fleeing and trying to run out of Room 3; is that right? Or if not, tell me what is right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that these men had started to flee towards Room --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Did you see them start to flee or did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: When did you see them start to flee, see the actual people fleeing? When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At night, because I didn't sleep for long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You woke up and then what? You saw them out of the bars of Room 1, you saw them fleeing? Is that what you're telling me now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know, in the morning when I got up, I saw two or three bodies on the spot where they were killed, and I carried them past Room 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand that, but I think just a few minutes ago you were asked the question by your own Defence counsel -- not your own Defence counsel, but Mr. Zigic's: "Did you see people running past the room during the shooting?" and you said no. So I am trying to make sure I understand. You saw those bodies of fleeing people the next morning, but did you ever actually see people fleeing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At night, during the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you're changing your testimony now to the extent that you're saying yes, you did see them at night during the shooting, while you were in Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this original episode in which Mr. Zigic saved your life, you said that another soldier threatened you, and he took you and escorted you back to your room and made sure that the other soldier didn't hurt you. Now, during that episode, did you ever see Mr. Zigic talk to that other soldier, say anything to him, or was it merely that by being with you that protected you, and he never actually spoke or said anything in your presence to the person who was threatening you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did say something to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what it was or did you just see him speak to the other person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the man taking a knife and wanting to slit my throat. And I ran off to Zigic and I said, "Zigic, this one wants to slaughter me." And then Zigic said to him, "Who told you to hurt him?" Zigic said to me, "Sit down there and have a cigarette. No one may hurt you." I was so afraid, I said to Zigic, "Please take me to my dormitory," and he did. He took me there. And Zigic said to him, to this soldier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You've straightened that out for me. I just have two more questions. One was: You told us that after one of the funerals of, I believe, a Serbian either soldier or guard - I don't remember which - Karlica, that some people went into -- called out Car from the dormitory and took him out and beat him, not Zigic, but, according to your testimony, someone took him out and beat him. Do you have any idea why they would go after Car for this particular policeman's -- as a result of this policeman's being killed? Was it just generally they were just mad or did they somehow connect Car with the person whose funeral they had just been at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had come back from the funeral drunk, and they called out Car to come out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Why Car? Why Car, to your knowledge? Do you have --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they had caught him with a machine-gun on him and they knew him. Car was involved in the attack on Prijedor from Brdo, because it was from there that the war was being waged, from Brdo. Both Kozarac, Rakovcani, and Carakovo, they were all involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: During the night of the killings and shootings, since you said that you were awakened by the shootings and you could see some things happening from inside Room 1 by looking out, was it -- were you able to see whether it was only machine-gun -- the machine-gun that was positioned in front of Room 3 that was shooting or whether the machine-gun that was in front of Room 1, or near the Banja Luka road? Was that shooting too or was it just the machine-gun shooting in front of Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the one in front of Room 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us that during your time in Keraterm you did not see Mr. Zigic ever abuse anybody, except for the one incident you told us about with Car. Did you ever hear reports from any other of the detainees that they had seen or knew about or been the victims of any abuses by Mr. Zigic? And in general, what did you hear about Mr. Zigic - Did they like him? Did they not like him? Were they afraid of him? Were they not afraid of him? - from other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I was not afraid of Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I know that. I'm asking what you heard from other detainees.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. I don't remember. It's a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Judge Wald. Witness DD/1, I also have a few questions. I should like to go back to the statement that you made, "Zigic, this one wants to kill me." How did you learn the name "Zigic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him for the first time when he gave me cigarettes. That's when we met, and I heard soldiers call him Zigic, and that is how I started calling him Zigic, when he first gave me a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The incident which prompted you to say, "Zigic, this one wants to kill me," did it happen before or after Mr. Zigic had given you a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. After that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question, to return to this incident with Car, who was running around in a circle. You said that the soldiers forced him to run in a circle. My question is the following: Was Zigic present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there just the first time, when Car was brought in. I didn't see him after that, as I was there in the compound, I was distributing food, and we would have visits. Your mother, father, brother, or sister could come and visit you and bring you food in bags. And then for a while food was prohibited, and then Zigic would bring bags of food and distribute them to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understand correctly your answer to my question, Zigic was present when he kicked that man, that Car, but you don't know whether he was present when Car was running around in a circle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there only when Car was brought in and when Zoran Zigic kicked him in the behind. After that, I didn't see Zoran Zigic, as I have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time went by between the moment Car arrived and the incident with the running around in a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four days. No, no. Car was brought in immediately, and immediately he started running. As soon as he was captured with a 53 machine-gun on him, he immediately started running round in a circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the two events, the arrival of Car and the running around in a circle, followed one another immediately in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Mr. Zigic was present when he arrived, but you don't know whether he was present when Car was ordered to run in a circle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw Car starting to run and I saw Zoran Zigic coming into the compound. He just gave him one kick in the behind. But there were a lot of soldiers around. I don't know their names, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling me now that Zigic was present when Car started running in a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/1 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would come in, and Car started running when the police brought Car in in a police van, having captured him with a machine-gun, and they put it on his shoulder and told him to run in a circle, and Zigic hit him just once. I was there, not more than 15 [Realtime transcript read in error "50"] metres away. I saw it all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Fifteen metres away. Correction, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Witness DD/1. I saw that Mr. Stojanovic had something to say. Mr. Stojanovic, would you like to make your observation now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The witness said "not more than 15 metres," but the transcript says "50 metres." However, with all due respect for His Honour Judge Riad, I had an objection, as it contained a conclusion that does not emanate from this testimony, that the witness and his brothers were separately treated. We will hear about his brothers, but from this witness all we heard was that what made them special was that they were saved from certain death on a number of occasions, not only by Zigic, but by others, if this can be considered special treatment. I think it is premature to make such a conclusion. I do apologise to Judge Riad, but I don't think that the question should have been put in that way to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, these interventions are allowed by us, but not to make allegations but to put a question to the witness. So if there is anything you wish to clarify with the witness, you should do so, but then the Prosecutor has a chance to cross-examine. This is not the point of giving you the floor to say this or that. We are in the process of presentation of evidence. This is not the time for making any submissions. So I'm telling you now and for the future: If you have an observation to make, you must do so in the form of a question put to the witness. That is all that I have to tell you. So what is the question that you would like to put to the witness following the questions put by His Honour Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would rather not tire Your Honours further. I think it would only be repeating things that the witness has already said. So we would stop there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you see from your own conclusion that your observation was inappropriate. Witness DD/1, we have concluded our questions. All of us - the Prosecution, the Defence, and the Judges - have had a chance to put questions to you. Thank you very much for coming. We wish you a safe journey home, and I will ask the usher to see you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic. I think you have some exhibits to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, indeed. We should like to tender this sketch as Exhibit D8/4A. We should like it to be admitted as an exhibit under that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking for the admission of D/4 -- 8/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, both sketches, certainly. The first had already been marked, and this is an additional exhibit now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these exhibits are admitted into evidence. We've come to the point when we are going to have a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Before the next witness is shown in, I think that this is a convenient moment to go into a matter rapidly, that is to say, the model of Keraterm. The information that I have available is that the model itself was never admitted into evidence, and the Keraterm model does not exist in this case. The model that exists is the Omarska camp model, not the Keraterm camp model. So once again, the information I was given is that that particular model, if it does exist, belongs to the Prosecution, to the OTP. They constructed it or designed it or whatever. Now, I don't know how the Prosecutor can convey that exhibit to the Defence; I don't know. But let us -- we must make a distinction because people tend to forget that the Prosecution, the OTP, is one -- that the OTP is one thing and that the Trial Chamber is another. So the Trial Chamber does not in fact have anything to do with the model; the model belongs to the office of the Prosecution. So it is up to the parties to resolve that issue, in my opinion. But, at any rate, as I brought this up and as I mentioned the OTP and the Prosecution, I should like to hear their response to see whether I have understood things correctly, so I shall give the floor to Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is my understanding that it was indeed the Office of the Prosecutor which commissioned both the Omarska and Keraterm models. I would like, if the Court will indulge me, to have an opportunity to speak to the lead counsel in the Keraterm case to find out its status. I think it would be inappropriate for me to commit an exhibit that perhaps is currently being used, with their having just started last week. And I will report back to the Chamber and I will indicate to the Chamber any concerns that we may have in this case as to its use at this stage, but I would ask only to have enough time to speak to Mr. Ryneveld. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At all events, I think that we have received information, and Ms. Mackintosh, would you give us the proper information, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACKINTOSH
utterances.text: The information from the legal officer on the Sikirica trial chamber is that the model is not currently in use.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I then, if possible till this afternoon's session, have an opportunity to speak with him to see what their anticipated use would be if it's not being brought in yet. I think we're running simultaneously with this Chamber timewise, and I shall look for him at the 1.00 break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Susan Somers. And I would like to reassert what I just said. It is up to the parties to hold contacts and to arrive at an agreement, because as you know, I personally and the Chamber does not have the power to command that the model be brought here. As we have heard, it belongs to a different section of the Tribunal. So all I can say is that I hope you will meet and discuss the matter. The Prosecution has presented its case and used photographs, but if we see that the model would be important, we shall look into the feasibility of having it here. Having said that, we can take up our proceedings where we left off, and I should like to ask the usher to introduce the next witness who is, Mr. Deretic? Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Mr. Zigic calls to the stand the second witness, under the pseudonym DD/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a protected witness. We shall have the blinds closed to enable the witness to be ushered into the courtroom. And I say that for the benefit of the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DD/2. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are now going to read the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. The usher is going to show you a piece of paper which should have your name on it. Please give us a yes or no answer as to whether it is in fact your name or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Witness DD/2, we're going to refer to you as DD/2 because of the protective measures you have requested. Thank you very much for coming, first of all. We are now going to give the floor to Mr. Deretic, who is going to ask you questions. Mr. Deretic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we begin - I'm sorry - just for clarification, could the Prosecution see the name written on that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Judges have seen it. You can see it. Please wait a few moments, Mr. Deretic. Mr. Saxon, may we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Deretic, I think you need to go into private session, do you not, for the witness' particulars?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now go into private session, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After the war began in the area of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I was in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know when the Serbs took over power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: On the 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When the takeover of power took place in Prijedor, were arms used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know when the attack on the town of Prijedor took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During the attack on Prijedor, were there any soldiers and policemen killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When this attack took place, where were you yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In Donja Puharska, at home.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you say Gornja or Donja Puharska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I said Donja Puharska.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes. Where is it? Is it in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What is the national composition of that settlement where your house was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Mostly Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After the attack on Prijedor, did you have any problems linked to the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was it all about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The army came and collected us all up for the camps, all of us who were over 60.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was that on that same day when Prijedor was attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what time of day this happened? When did the army come to fetch you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was around noon, about 12.00.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: We were taken out onto the streets and transferred to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How did they take you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: By bus.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were any other of your family members with you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: My brothers.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About two hours.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, there wasn't enough room, so we were taken back to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was that on that same day when you were taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, what happened to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who destroyed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, who? The army, who else.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Which army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you were taken to Omarska and Keraterm, were you told why you were being taken there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: All they told us was that we were taken there -- we were being taken there for questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you told what you would be questioned about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: To see whether we had taken part in the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know the name and surname of Zigic, Zoran?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Before you were brought to Keraterm, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When did you meet Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I met him after my arrival at Keraterm, three or four days after I got there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you saw him for the first time -- when did you see him for the first time? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did he have a cap on his head of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He had a red beret.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he had any characteristic things on him, any characteristic traits apart from that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes. His hand was bandaged.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: For how long did you see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Until mid-June.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: From your arrival in Keraterm up until the middle of June, as you say, how many times did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: You mean how many times?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see him several times, once, twice, three times, more times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him at all after mid-June.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I am asking you in the period between your arrival in Keraterm and until the end of June, in that time period, did you see Zoran Zigic during that period, and if so, how many times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you saw him for the first time in the Keraterm compound, can you remember whether he was with somebody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing in Keraterm, what Zoran Zigic was doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you meet Zoran Zigic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: With my brother.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How did you happen to meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I met him through my brother. My brother told me about Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You said that Zoran Zigic at that time had a bandage on his left hand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you notice that Zoran Zigic was wearing gloves without the tips of the fingers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you saw him for the first time, do you remember the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see him wearing an earring, perhaps, in his ears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you saw Zoran in the compound, what was his behaviour like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, he was behaving nicely.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How did he talk to others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Nicely.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After you were brought to the investigation centre of Keraterm, what room were you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you questioned, interrogated at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How many times were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How much after your arrival in Keraterm were you taken for investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you questioned immediately upon your arrival in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How much later were you questioned? How much time passed before you were taken for questioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About four or five days went by.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who questioned you in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were inspectors from Prijedor or Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember what the inspectors asked you about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: They asked us whether we had taken part in the attack on Prijedor and wanted to see if we had any weapons at home.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After you were questioned, what room were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Room 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Which room were your brothers in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: They were all together with me in Room 2 until they were interrogated. After the interrogation, they were placed in Room 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember in Room 2, was there a door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of door, that is to say, what was the door made of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was a tin, a metal door.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were there any apertures on the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In Room 1, was there a door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: There were bars, a net.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, did you -- would you see Zoran Zigic in the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see him during the day or during the night or both, during the day and the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Only during the day.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know a man or a person called Sead Jusufagic, also called Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How did you come to know him and since when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I knew him from before the war because he was a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where he lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In Raskovci, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is that, too, one of the suburbs of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you describe Car physically? What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was of medium height, he was fair, and he was skinny.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember, since you said you knew him from before, whether he had his teeth intact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of a person was Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He had big problems. He had problems with the police. Ever since his youth he was in correctional institutions.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
