utterances.text: Do you know whether he was ever convicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know whether Car was in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Car in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I didn't see him until he was brought there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When was Car brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: After my arrival there, three or four days after me.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When Car was brought to Keraterm, did you see him then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember how Car was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In a police van, a Black Maria.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was Car carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, he was: a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where Car was captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: At Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After Car was brought to Keraterm, do you know whether he was mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: As soon as he was taken out of the police van, they started hitting him immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you describe in some greater detail the event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: As soon as he was brought in, they started beating him straight away with the machine-gun. The soldiers caught him and put him in a circle to run around, carrying the machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you remember, within the Keraterm compound, where this took place exactly when Car was running around in a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In between number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "number 1" and "number 2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In the compound.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you mean the rooms or something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No. No. In the compound.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Within that group of soldiers that you saw when Car was brought in, was Zoran Zigic one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know who forced Car to run around in a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: As he was running, was Car carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was he carrying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: While Car was running around in a circle, was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: They hit him in any way they could as he was running around with the machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What did they hit him with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: With truncheons, they kicked him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: While Car was running around in a circle, did you see Zoran Zigic hitting Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I saw him hit him only once. He kicked him in the behind as he was running.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After this incident, did you see Car being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who beat him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The soldiers hit him. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was Zoran Zigic later on among the soldiers who were beating Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I didn't see him again.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Among the soldiers who were beating Car, did you know anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I only knew Banovic, Cupo.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is Cupo a name or a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: That's how they call him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know why they called him that? Did he have short hair, long hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He had long hair.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was Car beaten every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember a particular incident linked to the beating up of Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Car dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: When he was dead?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes. When did you see him dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: On the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you explain that a little? Does that -- are you giving us the exact date when you say "the 6th of the 7th," or do you mean the 6th and the 7th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: What I mean is that the 6th is the sixth month and the 7 is the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My concern is that Mr. Deretic is leading the witness, Your Honour. The witness needs to testify from his own memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I see in the transcript there's mention of the month of July. He said "the 6th" and "the 7th." He didn't say the month -- he didn't use the word "July." So I just want the witness to clear up the answer by giving us a proper answer to my question as to the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, there's always a matter of interpretation. What we see in the transcript is that the witness said the 6th of July. That's what we see.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness says not July, but June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I have received an explanation from the French booth. So both of you are right. Mr. Saxon is right and Mr. Deretic is right. The point is that we have interpreters between us. Perhaps this should be borne in mind. The interpreters tell me that yes, they heard the witness say 6th, 7, and it's up to Mr. Deretic to clear up the matter with the witness. Mr. Saxon's observation is justified, because he had his English version, and you have the original, the answer of the witness. With a little tolerance, we can achieve our goal. Please proceed, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the English interpreter explain that the B/C/S often use 6th for the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see on the transcript mention of the month of July, and from the witness' answer, that is not what he said. So that is why I put the question again to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic. Don't expand. We accept your apologies. But there is no need to apologise, because I don't think you offended anyone. So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So Witness DD/2, can you tell us: From the moment you saw Car arrive in Keraterm, how much time went by until the moment you saw him dead? So let us try and be even more precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A lot of time went by.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you give us the date when you saw Car dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was the sixth month and the seventh date, which means the 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. At what time of day did you see his body? Was it in the morning, at noon, or in the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember what preceded Car's death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was beaten non-stop.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After this incident of running around in a circle, did you ever see Zoran Zigic hit Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No. I said that he hit him only once, as soon as he arrived, while he was running.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was that person brought to the Keraterm investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you tell us roughly when this person was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was brought in on the 8th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where he was brought from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: From Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How was Emsud brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In a police van, a Black Maria.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know how they called Emsud when he arrived at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When Emsud was brought to Keraterm, was he carrying anything on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of rifle did he have?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer? The interpreter did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When Emsud was brought to Keraterm, was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was the name of the gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A Singapore gun, a Singapore rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know why it was called that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: How should I know? That's how they called it. They said he was captured with that rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When Emsud Bahonjic was brought to Keraterm, was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where was Emsud Bahonjic put when he was brought to the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was put in number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where Emsud Bahonjic was beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is that Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Emsud Bahonjic being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was he beaten in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know whether this person was ever taken to hospital during his stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you say he was not, do you know whether he was taken to hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who beat Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The soldiers and the reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you know any of those policemen from the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what the reason was that soldiers and policemen beat Emsud?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Because they caught him up there with a Singapore rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was beaten during the day or at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: During the daytime.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did Emsud Bahonjic die, or was he killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know that Zigic, Zoran, beat Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I never saw him beat him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, do you know a person called Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who was Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A policeman.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what his ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A Catholic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was he brought to this investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you tell us roughly when he was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I think he was brought about the same time as Emsud Bahonjic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember how he was dressed when he was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He had a police uniform on him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did he have anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What did he have on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A cap.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was there anything on that cap, an insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of a sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A five-cornered star.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Upon his arrival in Keraterm, do you know where Drago Tokmadzic was put up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Upon arrival in Keraterm, was he beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who beat Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The soldiers and the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know when he was beaten, during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Both during the day and during the night.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When Drago Tokmadzic was beaten during the night, were you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I couldn't see it when he was in number 2. All I could hear was the names being called out.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: His name was called out, Drago Tokmadzic. He was called to come out, and I just heard his moans.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you recognise by his voice the person calling out Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zoran Zigic beating Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: If Zoran Zigic had called him out at night, would you be able to recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I would be able to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did he ever call him out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He succumbed.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: On the 20th of June, June.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, were you in Keraterm when a massacre occurred one night when a large number of people were killed, detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was between the 24th and the 25th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When this event took place, in which room were you detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was that the room with the bars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Which room? Which room were you in when the massacre occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was there a tin metal door on that room or iron bars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: There was a tin door.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You explained a moment ago when I asked you about the doors that you were brought to Room 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Ah, I apologise. I thought you were asking me about number 3, the door to number 3, but the door to number 1 had bars on the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the transcript it says that it was Room 2, but the witness said that he thought I was asking him about Room 3, so may I ask the question again to clarify this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When the shooting took place and the massacre, which room were you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of door did that room have?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer? Could the witness please repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I was in Room 1, and the door had a net, a netting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: From that room, Room 1, could you see the compound in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At that time, how many rooms were there in which the detainees were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: There was Room 1, 2, 3, and 4.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In Room 3, where were the detainees from in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: From Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of day it was before the shooting and massacre took place? Was it a sunny day? Was it a rainy day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was a sunny day.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Keraterm was provided with any -- had any weapons to secure it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were these?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How many machine-guns were put up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I think there were two. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you locate those machine-guns? That is to say, could you tell us where they were positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: One of them was in front of Room 3.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What about the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The other one was to the right-hand side, by the weighing-in device.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not hear your answer. Where was the second machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: One of them was between 1, 2, and 3, that is to say, facing number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And what about the other one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The other one was by the fence, facing Room 1.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember since when those machine-guns were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see them being positioned on that particular day, placed there on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were those machine-guns put up that day before the shooting or were they there from earlier on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No. Those machine-guns were put there when the massacre occurred that night, prior to that happening.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What were the machine-guns placed on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: There was a barrier there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was the barrier made of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Sandbags.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know whether that night the compound was lighted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How was the compound lighted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: You mean when it was lighted? There was a power cut, and it was poorly lighted, because the light only came from the lampposts. You couldn't see properly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Does that mean that in the Keraterm compound there were lampposts with lights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, lampposts.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you remember how many lampposts there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I can remember two, seeing two.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: After midnight.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you remember before the shooting started that the guards cautioned those individuals, that they cautioned the people in any way? Did they caution them in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is leading. This is leading -- these are leading questions, Your Honour, or that last question, at least, was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, could you rephrase that question, ask what the conduct of them was, if you say what you said [as interpreted]. Please proceed, anyway, and rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was the guards' conduct towards the detainees prior to the actual shooting taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: They behaved well.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you say "well," do you mean that they behaved well to the detainees in Rooms 1, 2, 3, and 4, or do you just mean one of those rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I mean all the rooms.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: From the room you were in, could you see what was happening in front of Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When the shooting -- when did the shooting start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: At about midnight.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was shooting directed towards your room, the room you were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: From your room, could you see the machine-gun positioned in front of Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How far was it, the machine-gun? Can you tell us how far the machine-gun was from Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: On that day, that is to say, before it grew dark and before the shooting actually started, did you happen to see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see him after it got dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic moving around by the machine-gun from which the firing came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How long did the shooting last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It lasted two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In the morning, did you leave your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What time was it when you left the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About 6.00.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was your room -- before you left the room, was it locked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who let you out of the room, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was he doing in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was a guard. He would lock the door and unlock it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After you left the room, Room 1, what did you see in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A large number of dead and wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you left Room 1, did you happen to see in the Keraterm compound a truck of any kind, a Schlepper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you hear it come in, being brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know who the truck belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Whose trailer truck was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It belonged to AutoTransport.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It said so on the doors.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you left your room, where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was in front of Room 3.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How was the truck facing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It was facing in reverse.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see the driver of the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No. I just saw a civilian, a civilian driving it. I just saw that a civilian was driving the truck.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where was that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In the truck.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: On the occasion, did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what that truck was to be used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was it to be used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: For the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may we go into private session for a few moments, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can take advantage of this interruption. I think it is time to take our lunch break at this point. Is that convenient to you, Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us adjourn for lunch. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany the witness out of the courtroom first, and then we'll take a break. Witness, don't move for the moment while the blinds are being lowered. We adjourn for a 50-minute lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Usher, may we have the witness escorted into the courtroom, please. Witness DD/2, are you sitting comfortably and have you had a nice lunch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Deretic, I hope you are feeling comfortable as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, do you know which direction the tow truck was taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In an unidentified, unspecified direction.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During the day, did that tow truck return to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately at what time it returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About 11.00.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was it washed after it had returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who washed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you have any problems while you were doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I can. I was washing the truck, and a soldier came by. His name was Rajko. He wanted to kill me.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I called my brother to save me, and he called a policeman. His name was Cicic, and that Cicic came and took Rajko, that is to say, he threw him out of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: On that particular morning when you left Room 1 up until the time you began washing the truck and during the course of that whole day, did you happen to see Zoran Zigic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how and why you were washing the truck in the first place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Because it was all covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What did you wash it with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: With a hose and a brush.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After this event at Keraterm, how long were you in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Until the middle of August.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I went to Trnopolje. Not Keraterm, Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So, at the time when this event in Keraterm occurred with respect to the killing of those people up until your departure to Trnopolje, in that time interval, did you see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About 15 days.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic during that period ever in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, ever after June, after the middle of June 1992 up until the present day ever see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You spent, according to your testimony, about two and a half months in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During that period of time did you ever happen to see Zoran Zigic beat or beat up anybody or kill anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I should like to go back to a detail that you mentioned. When Zoran Zigic came to the Keraterm compound, did he, with respect to other people, in his conduct -- in his conduct, was he different? Did he shout? Was his behaviour different from the behaviour of the other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, yes, he would shout around a bit. He would make more noise.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who did he shout at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, he didn't shout at anybody in particular. He would just be loud and shout at all of us.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: While he was doing this shouting, was he shouting only at the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did he behave that way towards the soldiers and policemen as well, or rather, the guards in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 69, line 20 of the LiveNote, I asked the following question. I asked whether the witness had seen Zigic in Trnopolje, and in the transcript it says that he did not see him in Keraterm. So may I repeat the question, with your permission?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you, Witness, during your stay in Trnopolje, ever see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, did you last week have occasion to read an article which appeared in Blic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In that article it says that while Car was running around in the circle, Sead Jusufagic -- that is, several people beat him; amongst others, that one particular person beat him with a truncheon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, Mr. Saxon would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise. I have nothing I need to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. Please proceed, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am referring to the article I presented here yesterday. I think the Prosecution has received a photocopy of that article, so my question refers to that particular article, and I shall be brief.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever see, while Car was walking around in the circle, Zoran Zigic compel him to sit down on a beer bottle or mineral water bottle, that he made him take down his trousers and had to sit down on this mineral water bottle, and that is what, in fact, Car died of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever see, after that running around, Zoran Zigic and another man, as it says in the article, Duco, take Car off to another room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't know that man.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did Zigic take him off with a man to a room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Also in the article it says that the machine-guns were placed on school benches prior to the massacre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is it true that the detainees from Room 3 were not given food or water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, they were given food and water.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Would you please tell us: After you left Trnopolje -- that is to say, when did you leave Trnopolje? How long did you stay in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I stayed about 15 days.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What happened after you left Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After you left Trnopolje, did you spend your entire time in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Up until 1994, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where did you go in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I went to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In what entity is Travnik located? Is it the Serb entity or the Bosnia-Herzegovina entity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: It is Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is that entity controlled by the Serbs or Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you arrived in Travnik, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: When I arrived in Travnik, what happened was that they wanted to mobilise me into the army, me and my brother, and they put us in a barracks. And a soldier came and a policeman with him, and they called me out. They called me to go outside into the corridor, and I went outside because they suspected me. They thought that I had collaborated with the Serbs in 1992, so they threw me in prison, into a cell in Travnik, me and my brother, too. Then they began to beat us. They began beating us, me and my brother.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was that your older or younger brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: My older brother.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How long did you spend in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: One month.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After that, were you imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: You mean after Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I was transferred to Zenica to the prison there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How long did you spend in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: One year.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you convicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Finally at the end, I have three more questions for you. During the entire time that you were in Keraterm, who handed out the food and water to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: As we are in open session, don't mention names, please. Can you tell us when that brother of yours was assigned to hand out detainees food and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: During the day.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who told him to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Finally, can you tell us, please, why you came here -- agreed to come here to testify for an individual like Zoran Zigic who is charged with war crimes by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Because he saved my brother and because he helped me, too. He would give me two boxes of cigarettes when there was a shortage, and he would give me a bit of the food and some biscuits, and I decided to come forward and testify in favour of Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that concludes my examination of the witness for the time being. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Deretic. Mr. Saxon, your witness. Witness DD/2, you will be answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just one question before I begin, Your Honour. I have approximately 80 minutes, one hour and 20 minutes, for this cross-examination. Does the Trial Chamber intend to break right at 3.00, just so that I can plan the work that I'm going to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we ought to end by that time. Of course, there are additional questions, maybe, and the Judges' question time, so bear that in mind, please, and finish at three.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if we are to finish at three, will I have some time tomorrow morning, then, to finish the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Of course, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May we go into private session for a few minutes please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that we are in open session, so you can continue, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, have you always told the truth about your experiences in the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You're prepared to tell the whole truth about your experiences today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You briefly described your detention on the 30th of May, 1992, and I'd like to go back to that for a minute or two. Were you detained at home or outside of your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: While you and your brothers were being detained that day -- actually, let me step backwards for a moment. Do you have any sisters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: While you and your brothers were being detained that day, what was happening to your parents and to your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: They stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were they mistreated in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did anyone enter your home to speak with your parents and your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness said that on that day he was taken to Keraterm, so how can he know whether anybody came to his house after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: While I was there, nobody came. After I left, I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic. You are right in a certain aspect, but there is hearsay evidence as well. The witness might have learnt from somebody, and that somebody had come after he had left. So please continue, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Since you -- after you were detained, or since your detention in the Keraterm camp in the years since 1992, have you spoken to your parents and to your sister about the events of the day, the 30th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you and your brothers were detained, was anybody killed from your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: A neighbour.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall the names, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I can't say that name and surname now, when we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for a minute, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Why not? Let's go into private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Approximately how many men were detained with you from your neighbourhood that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: How can I know the number? How can I tell you when I don't know myself?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I used the term "approximately." Can you give an estimate, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: You mean those that went to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About three busloads. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How were you treated when you arrived at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The very moment when you arrived and you got off the buses you were treated well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was anybody on the buses with you beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did anybody have their valuables taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You've talked about the beating of different persons today already during your direct testimony. You've talked about the beating of the man known as Car, you've talked about the beating of a man named Emsud Bahonjic. Can you recall the names of any of the persons, whether they were guards or soldiers or visitors, who beat the detainees at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: We weren't beaten on the way to Keraterm and when we arrived at Keraterm, but once we were put up there, there were call-outs.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. Thank you for clarifying that. My question is: Can you recall today the names of any of the people who would call out detainees and beat them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Does the name Miso mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Does the name Zeljko Banovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Does the name Coric or Coro mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Oh, that's the one from Hadzija. His name is Coric, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Coric beat or mistreat anybody at the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What did you see Mr. Coric do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: When it was breakfast time in Keraterm, that was outside, and if someone had a good watch he would take it off, because they said you'd be called out in the evening. He took off gold and watches of many people.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Coric beat anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Coric from; do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Coric's first name or a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did other guards at the Keraterm camp take valuables from prisoners, like watches, or is it just Mr. Coric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you recall the names of some of the other guards who took valuables from the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, because it was many years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall the date when you were questioned or interrogated at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you beaten during your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, to your knowledge, who was the warden of the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I can't remember, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You've testified a bit about Zoran Zigic today. Regarding Mr. Zigic in particular, was he employed at the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He was there like a sort of guard.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Zigic behaved nicely in the Keraterm camp and that Mr. Zigic spoke to others nicely in the Keraterm camp. How many times did you actually see Mr. Zigic in the Keraterm camp? Just once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was that the day that the man known as Car was brought to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Zigic kick Car in the backside, did you hear Mr. Zigic say anything at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: There's something else I'd like to clarify from your direct testimony. You were taken to the Keraterm camp on the 30th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We haven't heard an answer, Your Honour. I don't know if the witness has answered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I didn't understand what you wanted me to say.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You were taken to the Keraterm camp on the 30th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, the man known as Car arrived there at Keraterm three to four days later, say around approximately the 3rd of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You said during your direct testimony that Car was beaten non-stop, and that he --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That Car was beaten non-stop until he died on the 7th of June, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes. Not July, June.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for clarifying that. Would it be fair then to say that Car was beaten over a period of three to four days before he died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember all those details because all that happened so long ago, nine years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: But you do recall that the beating of Car began three to four days after your arrival; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic was present at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Just the first time, and he hit him once in the backside when he was brought there. And I'm talking about Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During those days of non-stop beating of Mr. Car, how many times were you present while Car was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did the beating of Car continue when you went into your room, that is, Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you hear that beating going on from inside your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I just heard his moans.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You mentioned that Car died on the 7th of June. Why does that date stick in your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: He succumbed to his injuries on the 7th of June, 1992, but he wasn't taken away straight away for burial.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why that date has remained in your mind? Because you said a few minutes ago that it's been a long time and it's hard to remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You testified that a man named Emsud Bahonjic was beaten inside of Room 1. Was Emsud Bahonjic beaten in full view of the other prisoners detained within Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Only those in Room 1 where I was.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: About how many prisoners were detained in Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About 150 to 200.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier today that you never saw Zoran Zigic beat Emsud Bahonjic. Last year a witness known as Witness N testified in this courtroom about the beating of Emsud Bahonjic, and the witness known as Witness N describes Mr. Zigic forcing Emsud Bahonjic to sing songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I'm looking at page 3892 of the trial transcript, the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: According to Witness N, Mr. Zigic forced Emsud Bahonjic to sing songs, and while Emsud Bahonjic, Mr. Zigic -- while Emsud Bahonjic was singing, Mr. Zigic beat Emsud Bahonjic. According to Witness N, Mr. Zigic repeatedly kicked Emsud Bahonjic and beat him with his pistol. Can you comment as to why your testimony, since you were also in Room 1, differs so greatly from the testimony of Witness N?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: All I know is that Zigic did not beat Emsud Bahonjic, nor did he force him to sing. There were a lot of soldiers and policemen around there. I don't know who it was who forced him to sing. They did beat him in Room 1, this Bahonjic. I don't know what happened to him later on.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Zigic present while Emsud Bahonjic was being beaten in Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You talked about a man named Drago Tokmadzic, and you testified that Drago Tokmadzic's ethnicity was Catholic. Does that mean that Drago Tokmadzic was also a Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, you were confined in Room 1, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Drago Tokmadzic was confined in Room 2; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You testified that when Drago Tokmadzic was called out at night and beaten, you could hear his moans, but if I understand you, you couldn't actually see the beating of Drago Tokmadzic that was going on. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see it, but I did hear him being called out, and I heard his moans, his voice, because he was alone outside. I don't remember who beat him; soldiers and policemen, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So you couldn't see who was beating Drago Tokmadzic, could you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you tell by the sounds whether Drago Tokmadzic was being beaten by one person or by a group of persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No, I can't remember whether there was one or two or five of them.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you see in the dark who was calling out Drago Tokmadzic? Was it -- well, my first question is, could you see who was calling out Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you see whether just one person was calling out Mr. Tokmadzic, or whether there was a group of persons waiting for Mr. Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: There was one person calling out, and I think a group of men were waiting for him, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions to ask you about the shooting that occurred of the prisoners in Room 3 at Keraterm, and I need to clarify something with you. During your direct testimony you were asked when the machine-guns were set up at Keraterm, and I believe that you said that the machine-guns were put there when the massacre occurred, that is, prior -- your words were "prior to that happening." Are you saying that the machine-gun was placed outside of Room 3 during the day before the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, if the shooting began sometime after midnight, can you recall approximately how long before the shooting began or around what time of day was that machine-gun set up outside of Room 3, noontime, 3.00 in the afternoon, 6.00 in the afternoon? Can you give even an estimate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: About noon when it was put opposite number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were only two lampposts with lights in the Keraterm compound. Were any extra lights set up before the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You said that prior to the shooting that day, that the guards behaved well with respect to the detainees, that they treated the detainees well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: If the guards were trying to treat the detainees well, why do you suppose they set up a machine-gun and pointed it at Room 3 that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: In Room 3, it was very hot, and people couldn't stand it any more so they started fighting amongst themselves. They started breaking down the door to escape, and the guards pushed them back. They tried -- started running everywhere and then they opened fire, because there was a metal door there. This was in the evening, after midnight.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So just so I understand you, Witness DD/2, is it your testimony today that the guards just happened to set up a machine-gun at noontime on the 24th of July pointing at Room 3, and later that night around midnight, the prisoners, just by coincidence, began to escape? Is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Very well. In 1994, Witness DD/2, did you give a statement to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina about your experiences in the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Would you agree that your memory about the events of 1992 was fresher in 1994 than it is today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/2
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for a few minutes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we're going into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday, the 29th day of March, 2001, at 9.20 a.m.
